extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy members, submitters, Voting Members, Chapter leaders, and GRAMMY Awards participants
extracted.subtask_description: Official Recording Academy rules governing committee composition, nomination and voting procedures, credit-change policies, For Your Consideration (FYC) marketing rules, voter conduct, and who is recognized as a nominee/winner for GRAMMY categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee membership documentation for Craft judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Each candidate for Craft Committee membership must be a Voting Member of the Academy in the membership class that corresponds to the Craft they are being submitted to judge and must fill out a Documentation Form listing six tracks or albums for which they have the nomination-eligible credit corresponding to the Craft. The credits must be for recordings released in the previous five years. The form remains on file at the National Office of the Recording Academy and is valid for five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation establishes eligibility to serve on Craft Committees; the six items must match the Craft credit being used to qualify. The form's five-year validity period governs how long the documented eligibility remains on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Populating Craft Committees and ratification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Chapter’s Executive Director develops a slate of recommendations with the Chapter Nominating or Executive Committee and Chapter President; recommendations can be supplemented by the CEO and National Chair in consultation with Awards and Craft Committee Chairs for DEI and balance considerations. The final slate is submitted to the National Board of Trustees for ratification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee membership is driven by Chapter proposals with oversight to ensure diversity, equity, inclusion and balance; ultimate ratification by the Board centralizes final approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum consecutive service and chair service limits
rubrics_metrics.description: No person would serve for more than five consecutive years without a break. If a committee member is selected to chair, they may serve up to an additional three consecutive years. Committee members may serve a maximum of eight consecutive years if they served on the committee first and were then elected to be chair. Two years off would still apply in these cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service term rules include both member and chair sequences; 'two years off' is required after reaching service limits before serving again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum committee turnover requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 25% of each committee must turn over from the previous year’s committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This turnover requirement is applied to maintain renewal and prevent entrenchment; further specifics note 25% turn over each year by the fourth year in multi-year service cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination process for Best Historical Album
rubrics_metrics.description: This Category is voted on by a National Craft Nominating Committee. The committee of 25 Voting Members meets to judge all the entries made in the Category and vote by confidential individual ballot to select the five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Craft Nominating Committee convenes in person (or as specified) to view entries and cast confidential ballots; committee size specified as 25 Voting Members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-round process for Instrumental Composition/Arrangements/Producer of the Year (Non-Classical)
rubrics_metrics.description: First round of voting is by the General Voting Membership via the first ballot. The second round takes place in a National Craft Nominating Committee: the top 30 selections from the General Voting Membership in each Category (in Producer Of The Year, the top 30 Producers’ entered work — usually up to 90 titles) appear on the ballot for National Craft Nominating Committees (25-35 Voting Members) to vote by confidential ballot to select the five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system uses a broad first-round membership filter and a specialized national committee for final nomination selection; committee membership represents all Chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical multi-stage selection
rubrics_metrics.description: First round voting by the General Voting Membership via the first ballot and a committee vote of each of the Chapter Engineering Committees (twelve five-person committees) determine the Selections List. The second round takes place in the twelve Chapter Craft Committees. The Selections List (top 30 from the first-round member vote plus up to five selections from each of the twelve Chapter Committees) appears on the ballot for the Chapter Committee members to vote by individual confidential ballot to determine the five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category combines member-wide voting with chapter-level engineering committee inputs to produce a Selections List; chapter committees then choose final nominees via confidential ballots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer of the Year (Classical) and certain Classical categories process
rubrics_metrics.description: For Producer of the Year, Classical; Best Engineered Album, Classical; and Best Contemporary Classical Composition, the first round of voting is by the General Voting Membership via the first ballot. The second round takes place in National Craft Nominating Committees. The top 30 selections from the General Voting Membership appear on the ballot for the National Craft Nominating Committees to vote by confidential ballot to select the five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar two-round structure as other categories but specifies classical-focused categories and national committee handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Committee standard operating details (selections list, terms, turnover)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Craft Committee receives a list of 30 titles from the first round of voting by the membership (or possibly more to account for ties). Committee Members serve five years on and one year off; Committee Chairs serve three years on and two years off. 25% turn over each year by the fourth year. Committees are populated the same way current Craft Committees are, with names proposed from Chapters, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specifics on how many items appear on committee ballots, standard member/ chair term cycles, and turnover expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Craft Nominating Committees for Package categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Recording Package and Best Boxed/Special/Limited-Edition Package meet in Regional Craft Nominating Committees to view and judge all entries made in the Categories and vote by confidential ballot to select the five nominations. This is similar to Composition/Arrangement and Producer Of The Year (Non-Classical) but does not involve the General Voting Membership first ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These package categories are handled regionally and do not use the general membership-first round; committees view all entries and vote confidentially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Album Notes National committee remote voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Album Notes is voted by a single National Craft Nominating Committee of 30-50 Voting Members. This committee does not meet in person; members access a password-protected section of the Academy website to view all Notes entries and vote by individual, confidential ballot to determine the five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote review and confidential individual voting is authorized for this category; committee sizes and procedures are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Immersive Audio Album committee eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are selected by a committee of 20–25 Voting Members. To be eligible to serve on this committee, one must be a Voting Member in good dues standing, meet certain qualifications in the Engineering or Producing fields, and be approved by the Trustees. The committee reviews all Immersive Audio Album entries in their meeting and votes individually for the final five nominees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee membership requires technical qualifications plus Trustee approval; committee conducts full review of entries and individual confidential votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songwriter of the Year (Non-Classical) nominating committee process
rubrics_metrics.description: The national Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical Nominating Committee is comprised of diverse and 'highly relevant' songwriters. The committee meets once, is given the voters’ top 30 selections from first-round voting (alphabetical by songwriter), is provided submitted material (recordings and lyrics), and each committee member votes by individual confidential ballot to determine the final nominees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee membership emphasizes relevance and diversity; committee bases decisions on submitted recordings and lyrics for the songwriters on the top-30 list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Video & Music Film nominating committee eligibility and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: First round of voting is by the General Voting Membership; second round is by a National Craft Nominating Committee of 16–20 Voting Members balanced between video and film. The top ~30 selections from the General Voting Membership appear on the committee ballot. Committee members must document six music videos or three music films to be eligible. Committee Chairs are chosen each year by confidential majority vote from the previous Craft Committee. The committee meets two days in person in an appropriate screening room/venue, reviews the top 30 selections entirely, discusses each project, and votes confidentially on the five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies eligibility documentation for committee service, chair election method, in-person screening environment, and confidential ballot voting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination Change Request Policy — initial submission acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission, the submitter receives a list of names they have submitted as eligibly credited and must acknowledge the list is complete; it may not be changed without additional qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters bear responsibility to verify credits at submission; changes are restricted and require documented justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-nomination announcement credit-change requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: After the submission period is closed and before the nominations announcement, submitter may send changes in the credits with required documentation: (1) Affidavit that the change request has been verified to be true; (2) Reason for the change; (3) Submit updated (final) label copy; (4) Confirmation that the credits have been updated across DSPs as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented evidence and label copy are necessary to modify credits prior to nominations announcement; changes are not automatic and must meet documentation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for credit corrections before the telecast (post-announcement, two-week window)
rubrics_metrics.description: After nomination announcement, submitter may request changes within two weeks with required documentation: (1) formal statement from head of label/content owner/producer detailing inaccuracies and corrective steps; (2) notarized artist statement where applicable; (3) updated approved label copy or credit list; (4) call sheets or studio logs proving additional person(s) worked on recording and roles; (5) payment of $200 fee per added name in advance; (6) confirmation that credits updated across DSPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict evidence requirements and an advance fee apply for post-announcement/pre-telecast credit additions; multiple corroborating documents expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for credit corrections after the telecast (one-year window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual not included in the Final Nominations List who claims a nomination after the deadline will be informed that official changes will be done after the awards telecast. There is a one-year deadline from the telecast to request crediting changes/additions to nominated or winning albums; required documentation is the same as pre-telecast. There is a $200 fee per added name payable in advance and confirmation that credits have been updated across DSPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-telecast changes are allowed within one year with same documentation and fee; after one year, requests go to the Executive Committee and are discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-one-year credit-change escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the one-year deadline, any request for changes must be made to the Executive Committee of the Board of Trustees. The requesting party is responsible for providing all necessary documents to show proof of claim and it will be at the sole discretion of the Executive Committee whether to consider the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late claims are exceptional, require full documentation, and are handled at Executive Committee discretion — decisions are not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges to GRAMMY Award entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions regarding GRAMMY Award entitlement are made by the Awards Department. Any challenge to a final entitlement decision shall be made in writing and addressed to the Executive Committee of the Recording Academy. The Executive Committee is empowered to investigate, consider and decide the challenge and shall have the authority to act with the power of the Board of Trustees for that purpose. The Executive Committee’s decision shall be communicated in writing and shall be final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal written challenge process routed to Executive Committee; committee has investigatory and final decision authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of nominations any nominee may receive (Rules A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several rules govern how many nominations an individual Artist may receive: RULE A: 1 nomination only. RULE B: No limit on number of nominations. RULE C: 1 nomination to the Artist with exceptions allowing 2 nominations under specified co-nominee conditions. RULE D: 1 nomination per music video or music film. RULE E: 1 nomination with exceptions allowing 2 if the Artist is different. FOR CLASSICAL: 1 nomination with various exceptions allowing 2 under certain orchestra/co-nominee/choral conditions. RULE F: 2 nominations as follows: combinations of individual and co-nominations as enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies across categories with specified exceptions; consult category-specific rule assignments (A–F) to determine limits for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-to-rule mapping (number of nominations by category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Category is mapped to a rule letter (A–F) indicating nomination limits. The document lists many categories (Record Of The Year (C), Album Of The Year (C), Song Of The Year (B), Best New Artist (A), Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical (A), Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical (A), and many genre-specific categories) with footnotes indicating exception conditions (e.g., '* Rule C if Artist is nominee; * Rule B if Producer is nominee; * Rule A if Artist is nominee; * Rule E if Conductor is nominee and orchestra is different').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine allowed nominations for a person on a specific category, locate the category’s assigned rule letter and apply that rule together with any footnoted exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter Code of Conduct — impartiality and influence restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not allow their choices to be suggested, directed or influenced by anything other than their own analysis of merit, including but not limited to: personal friendships, company loyalties, regional preferences, or sales volume/popularity. Voters shall not accept money or anything of value in exchange for votes, access to other members, submission privileges, or any other membership privileges. Voters shall not enter into any agreements or understandings on how to vote, including 'Voting Blocs' or 'Vote Trading'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibitions on factors that could bias voting and on quid-pro-quo or organized vote arrangements; violations subject to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving integrity and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recording Academy may take corrective actions, including disqualification of entries, against any activity determined to undermine Academy guidelines. Any member who has authorized, executed or enabled a voting solicitation activity that undermines the Academy's regulations may be subject to suspension or termination of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement is broad and may include membership disciplinary actions and entry disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final voting and confidentiality of tabulation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the announcement of nominations, the final ballot is made available to all current Voting Members to select GRAMMY winners. All ballots, including those from special committees, are tabulated confidentially by an independent accounting firm. Results of the final voting are not known until the day of the GRAMMY Awards, when Deloitte delivers sealed envelopes with names of the winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final tallies are managed externally and kept confidential until telecast; members should not expect earlier disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescindment of GRAMMYs and absence of ranked results
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRAMMY process does not produce a ranked result with winner and ordered runners-up. If a GRAMMY Award is withdrawn following the presentation, no award is given in that Category for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no runner-up promotion if a winner is rescinded; rescindment results in vacated award for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: FYC proprietary information and permitted uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers specific to an official awards Category, Field and/or balloting, entry lists, and finals lists are proprietary information belonging to the Recording Academy and may not be used, disclosed, published, or otherwise distributed in connection with any FYC event, advertisement or for any other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if FYC events/screenings/ads are allowed, official Academy balloting data must not be repurposed or disclosed externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted content for FYC communications and advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: FYC communications may include: artwork related to product under consideration; brief, unembellished descriptions of the recording or creators; copies or links to product; links to websites that promote eligible recordings; link to Recording Academy website where Voting and Solicitation Guidelines are posted; lists of the creators who worked on the recording; reference to nominations once announced (list Category(s) by full name); reference to the GRAMMY Award with proper registered marks (limited usage rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications must include an opt-out option and are restricted to promoting only one's own recordings; the Academy does not release member contact information so vendors claiming lists are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content in FYC communications and advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: FYC communications cannot: cast a negative or derogatory light on competing recordings; exaggerate or overstate merits; include any Recording Academy trademarks or logos (logo use reserved for paid sponsors/partners); include entry list numbers or Category numbers; include chart numbers, number of streams, sales figures, or RIAA awards; include personal signatures/pleas to listen; misrepresent honors or awards; reference the year or the telecast number (e.g., '2024' or '67th GRAMMY Awards').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibitions aim to prevent lobbying, misrepresentation, or use of proprietary Academy identifiers; violations may result in removal/penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billboard GRAMMY Issue mailing and advertising restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording Academy members receive a complimentary copy of the Billboard GRAMMY Issue unless they opt out. Featured subjects/content determined independently of the Academy. The independent mailing house has signed an NDA; the Academy does not disclose member contact information to Billboard. Any member can take out an advertisement; advertising restrictions listed for FYC communications apply. Special rates exist for independent creators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party mailing handled under NDA; advertisers must still obey Academy FYC restrictions; contact membership@recordingacademy.com for ad rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting FYC events — hospitality and gifting restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent FYC events, programs or activities may be hosted if they adhere to the guidelines. FYC activities may not include any complimentary meals, alcoholic beverages, gifts, or any other hospitality that could be inferred as a value in exchange for vote consideration. Anything considered by the Recording Academy, in its sole discretion, as unreasonable promotion or gifting is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No hospitality that could be seen as inducement; host must avoid any offering that may constitute vote-buying or undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attending FYC events — ticket purchase requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If members are invited to a ticketed FYC event or program, they must purchase tickets at full price (no comps or discounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits comping or discounted admission for members to avoid perceived influence or indebtedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifting show tickets policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Widespread gifting of show tickets to members as part of an explicit or implicit FYC/vote solicitation campaign is not allowed. Chapters may not be used as a conduit for gifting to members, Governors and/or Trustees. Tickets not acquired by members through personal affiliations must be purchased at full price (no comps or discounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual talent can provide tickets via personal affiliations, but organized/generic gifting aimed at members is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy office mailings prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any mailing of FYC product or marketing materials to any of the Recording Academy offices is prohibited and will not be distributed to members, Governors or Trustees; such mailings will be disposed of or returned to sender at the Academy’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send promotional materials to Academy offices as they will not be distributed and may be discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone lobbying prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting Academy members by phone to promote a GRAMMY-eligible product or achievement is prohibited, even if such contact is in the guise of checking delivery of a sample product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phone calls intended to promote eligible product are banned regardless of stated purpose; use written opt-out-compliant communications instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party solicitation and vendor access restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no marketing companies authorized to have access to Recording Academy member lists or staff. If a vendor obtained, through wrongful conduct, an accurate member list, any entry that used the vendor’s services will be disqualified. Marketing companies may not use subscriber-based publications to distribute promotional materials to an Academy member unless the member is a subscriber (defined as having intentionally requested the publication be sent to them regularly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendors claiming access to member lists are likely fraudulent; use caution and report suspicious vendors. Unauthorized vendor usage can lead to entry disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy FYC website feature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For Your Consideration promotional listings are available on RecordingAcademy.com free of cost for entries accepted as official. The feature duration is the first-round voting period only. Members with accepted entries may post a link or upload their entries once in each approved FYC Category as specified in the Entry List. Duplicate posts, posts in the wrong Category, and promoting entries outside the For Your Consideration groups are violations; content will be removed and repeated violations may incur penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Academy’s official FYC feature for fair exposure; adhere to single-post-per-category rule and correct categorization to avoid content removal/penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy membership-hosted activity restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: GRAMMY-submitted product cannot be the topic of any Recording Academy Voting Member activity or promotion. Anyone who submitted product for awards consideration during the then-current voting cycle will not be featured by the Recording Academy at Voting Member events, in social media, or in recorded/streaming content where it may be perceived as promoting an eligible product. Talent not submitting product are eligible to participate in Academy activities. Once product has been submitted, FYC product distribution at Academy-hosted events is prohibited; violators will be asked to leave and may face penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academy-hosted events must remain neutral with respect to current-cycle submissions to prevent institutional promotion of eligible recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: FYC information contact and reporting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For further information contact 877.637.6816 / awards@recordingacademy.com. It should not be assumed that tactics not specifically prohibited are acceptable. The Academy will review materials or answer questions in advance and encourages reporting violations to the same contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, seek advance review from Awards staff; report suspected violations to help enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: GRAMMY Nominee, GRAMMY Winner, and Certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: GRAMMY Nominees: individuals eligibly credited on a GRAMMY-nominated recording for a nomination-eligible role are GRAMMY Nominees; they receive invitation, nominee ticket information, medallion and Nominee Certificate. GRAMMY Winners (Statuette): roles listed under Statuette are GRAMMY winners on winning projects and receive a statuette; list includes Nominees on the winning project and other roles recognized with statuettes (e.g., producers/engineers who worked on >50% of playing time in certain genre album categories). Certificates: Individuals on a GRAMMY-winning recording whose roles are listed under Certificate receive a Winners Certificate but are not Nominees or Winners. Participation Certificates can be ordered for a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who is a Nominee vs Winner vs Certificate recipient depends on category-specific role listings and percentage-of-playing-time rules for some album categories; Participation Certificates available for other contributors for a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific nominee/statuette/certificate allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: The document provides a detailed table mapping each Genre and Category to which roles are considered NOMINEE, which receive a STATUETTE (winners), and which receive a CERTIFICATE. Examples: Record Of The Year — Artist(s) & Producer(s), Engineer/Mixer(s), Mastering Engineer(s) (if other than Artist(s)) are Nominees and Statuette recipients. Album Of The Year — Artist(s) (including Featured Artists), Songwriter(s) of new material, Producer(s), Recording Engineer(s), Mixer(s) & Mastering Engineer(s) with >20% playing time are Nominees and Statuette recipients. Many genre-specific entries follow with percentage thresholds and special group rules (e.g., large ensembles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the category table to determine precisely which roles receive nomination recognition, statuettes, or certificates; footnotes indicate special rules (e.g., thresholds, conductor/orchestra exceptions, group-size rules).
